name: plesk-deploy-mcp
description: Set up and operate safe, approval-gated deployments to Plesk servers with GitHub Actions and automatic rollback.
long_description: Packages the plesk-deploy workflow for any agent. Local tools inspect a project, generate a deploy kit (a GitHub Actions workflow with an approval gate, a release manager that switches releases atomically, migrates safely, health-checks and rolls back by itself, and an idempotent server set-up) as a dry-run diff, and validate it. Optional SSH tools, off until you list your own ~/.ssh/config host aliases, read deploy status and logs and roll back. No tool accepts or returns a secret; deploys always go through GitHub Actions with a person approving. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Plesk or WebPros.

tools.name: inspect_project
tools.description: Read a project and return a Deployment facts table (verified or unknown); env variable names only.

tools.name: server_discovery_commands
tools.description: The read-only commands for the user to run on the Plesk server and paste back.

tools.name: generate_deploy_kit
tools.description: Render the deploy kit as a dry-run diff; write only when asked, never overwriting unlisted files.

tools.name: validate_deploy_kit
tools.description: Check the kit: shell syntax, workflow safety, the release manager's test suite, secrets.

tools.name: server_discover
tools.description: Run the fixed read-only discovery commands over your own SSH (opt-in), secrets redacted.

tools.name: deploy_status
tools.description: List the releases on the server and which one is live (opt-in SSH).

tools.name: deploy_logs
tools.description: Read the end of the release manager's deploy log (opt-in SSH).

tools.name: rollback
tools.description: Make the previous good release live again; needs an exact confirmation (opt-in SSH).

tools.name: github_deploy_runs
tools.description: Read the status of recent Deploy to Plesk runs from the GitHub API (read-only).

ssh_hosts.title: Allowed SSH host aliases
ssh_hosts.description: Comma-separated Host aliases from your ~/.ssh/config that the server tools may reach, e.g. myserver. Leave empty to keep the SSH tools off. Your ssh-agent and known_hosts are used; no key or password is ever entered here.

github_token.title: GitHub token (optional, read-only)
github_token.description: Only for github_deploy_runs on a private repository: a fine-grained token with Actions: read and Metadata: read on that repository.
